Executive Summary: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project focuses on the production of high-quality, nutrient-dense tomato powder using sustainable, efficient processing methods. By harnessing local agricultural resources and leveraging innovative drying techniques, the project aims to reduce post-harvest loss, enhance food preservation, and provide a value-added product for both local and international markets. This initiative seeks to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, create job opportunities, and contribute to sustainable food systems while addressing global food security.
Innovation Description: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project addresses the significant issue of tomato post-harvest loss, which is a widespread problem in many agricultural regions, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. Tomatoes are highly perishable, and poor storage, transportation, and handling contribute to up to 50% of losses annually. This results in wasted resources, financial losses for farmers, and limited availability of nutritious food.  The innovation provides a sustainable solution by turning fresh tomatoes into a long-lasting, nutrient-rich tomato powder. This method not only preserves the tomatoes but also adds value by creating a versatile product that can be used in cooking, food processing, and other industries. The drying process reduces water content, extending shelf life and making the product easier to store and transport.  The solution is driven by a combination of sustainable farming practices and modern drying technology, which retains the tomatoes' flavor, nutritional content, and versatility. It offers a win-win for both consumers and farmers. For consumers, it provides an affordable and convenient option for accessing high-quality tomatoes year-round. For farmers, it opens new markets and increases their income by offering a value-added product that can be sold locally and internationally.  The immediate benefits include reduced food waste, improved food security, and increased incomes for local farmers. Long-term, the initiative will contribute to sustainable agricultural practices, climate resilience, and greater access to affordable, nutritious food, helping improve the livelihoods of communities and creating positive environmental impacts.

Project Title: ICTs, market access and food security for small-scale fisheries
Executive Summary: ABALOBI empowers small-scale fishers to adapt to climate change through digital tools, sustainable practices, and community food security initiatives. Our programme channels affordable, high-quality seafood to vulnerable communities, expands distributor networks, and trains fishers in sustainability and digital tools. Tailored workshops empower women and marginalized groups, ensuring equal access to opportunities. Together with the ABALOBI Marketplace, these initiatives enhance traceability, foster socio-economic resilience, and promote sustainable resource use, strengthening livelihoods and marine health
Innovation Description: Small-scale fisheries provide jobs to 60 million people (representing 90% of the total global fishing industry) and support over 160 million jobs in ancillary activities. In Africa, they account for 85% of all fishers, feeding over 200 million people annually. Yet, these fishers, especially women who are vital to the sector, face systemic marginalisation in markets and management forums. Many earn less than $1 per day, lack access to financial services, and remain unseen in governance due to insufficient data and digital identities. This exclusion leaves them vulnerable to exploitative practices, trapping them in cycles of debt and poverty. ABALOBI addresses these barriers with an innovative combination of digital tools and tailored training programmes. Fishers gain digital identities to record, track, and market their catches transparently, bridging critical data gaps and unlocking access to fair markets, financial tools, and governance platforms. Women and marginalised groups are empowered through tailored workshops and mentorships, ensuring equal access to opportunities. Training on sustainable fishing techniques and digital tools builds capacity for ecosystem-friendly practices, leading to healthier fish stocks, reduced ecological footprints, and greater resilience to climate change. To further address food security, ABALOBI channels affordable, high-quality seafood into vulnerable coastal and rural communities, expanding coverage through a growing network of trained distributors. This integrated approach delivers immediate benefits: improved incomes, financial inclusion, and food security. Long-term, ABALOBI fosters socio-economic resilience, sustainable fisheries, and ensures small-scale fishers play a pivotal role in tackling global food security and safeguarding marine ecosystems.
